# A shared ambient facet extremal class and its ownership stress

This is a separate finite-complexity extremal class. It does not assume that
mixed cap ratios are convex under Minkowski addition. It proves no numerical
upper bound on a circuit's multiplier sum.

## 1. The closed finite-complexity class

Fix a finite lattice-convex P with z0 in the relative interior of conv(P),
and work with compatible actual compact convex fibers K_z. Normalize
vol_d(K_z0)=1. Fix N. Require that all the POSITIVE-volume fibers admit one
shared representation

    K_z={x: n_f.x+a_f.z<=b_f, 1<=f<=N},

with nonzero continuous n_f. Zero-volume fibers are permitted without a
facet-complexity requirement. This relaxed class is closed under the
Hausdorff convergence supplied by fixed-nonhollow-projection-compactness.md.

To prove this, pass to a subsequence on which all approximants' positive
index sets are the same. Every positive limiting index belongs to this set.
Normalize each n_f to unit length, allowing repeated and redundant planes,
and pass to subsequences n_f,l -> n_f and

    t_f,l(z)=b_f,l-a_f,l.z -> t_f(z) in R union {+infinity}

at each positive limiting fiber. The value -infinity is impossible, since
that limiting fiber has a uniform interior ball and all approximating fibers
stay uniformly bounded. For each f, the finite limiting thresholds belong
to the image of the finite affine evaluation map, which is a closed linear
subspace. Thus they can be realized by one affine threshold function.

In fact the intersection of the FINITE limiting inequalities at a positive
index z is exactly K_z, globally in R^d. One inclusion is immediate. For the
other, take any point y satisfying those finite inequalities and an interior
point q of K_z. A fixed ball around q is eventually in every approximating
K_z,l. Consequently, for 0<s<1, (1-s)y+s q satisfies all finite limiting
inequalities strictly. All divergent positive thresholds are eventually
larger than this fixed point's continuous evaluation. Hence this convex
combination belongs to K_z,l for all sufficiently large l. Hausdorff
convergence, followed by s down to zero, places y in K_z. This also proves
that the finite limiting inequalities already give a bounded set.

The affine-threshold saturation lemma from
candidate b989614dc4f86228 now realizes all finite values
and makes all positive-infinity entries arbitrarily large at the remaining
positive indices, without changing the finite values. Choose those entries
larger than the continuous support bounds of K_z. They are redundant there.
The resulting N actual ambient inequalities represent all positive limiting
fibers exactly. Thus the class is closed.

The fixed-P compactness theorem makes it compact modulo the permitted
fiber-affine normalization. Therefore maximum depth attains its minimum in
this class. A finite ambient-polytope inner approximation of a strict
counterexample supplies a finite N with a strict minimizer. The usual
alternative remains: either a zero-volume index can be removed with depth
unchanged, or the minimizer has all fibers positive.

From now on assume this latter branch. Fix a representation by N shared
planes. Small arbitrary perturbations of their coefficients keep every
finite P fiber positive and bounded. They automatically preserve convex
compatibility, since they still describe the sections of one convex
polyhedron over conv(P). Common continuous-affine normalization preserves
N. Hence these perturbations are legitimate competitors in the attained
extremal problem, with normalization restored afterwards if needed.

## 2. Nonsmooth objective derivatives and owner allocations

Distinct ambient planes can restrict to the same facet F of an integer
fiber. This cannot be ignored. Normalize every original continuous plane
normal to unit length. Write O(z,F) for its owners: those ambient planes
whose restrictions support K_z at F. All their continuous normals equal
the actual outward unit normal n_F. For an infinitesimal plane variation,
define its outward velocity at x in F by

    r_f(z,x)=delta b_f-delta a_f.z-delta n_f.x.

The actual fiber boundary velocity is

    r(z,x)=min_(f in O(z,F)) r_f(z,x).

Therefore the directional derivative of total mixed volume is

    M'(delta)=sum_(z,F) integral_F min_f r_f(z,x) dH_(d-1)(x).

This follows by the local swept-prism formula. Intersections of different
facet directions contribute only o(t); boundedness and the finite plane
list make the integrated remainder o(t) for each fixed variation.

Let omega_f(z,x)>=0 be measurable owner allocations, zero outside O(z,F),
with sum_f omega_f=1 almost everywhere on each facet. Then

    M'(delta)=min_(omega) L0,omega(delta),
    L0,omega(delta)=sum_(z,F,f) integral_F omega_f r_f.

The minimum is attained by choosing the first minimizing owner in the
finite owner list. The resulting gradient set G0 is compact and convex in
the finite parameter space: only masses and first moments of the bounded
allocation measures enter, and domination plus the partition-of-unity
condition is preserved under weak limits. G0 is thus a rigorously defined
set of objective gradients, not one falsely assumed differentiable gradient.

## 3. Cap derivatives with consistent section and ownership traces

Use the compressed circuit groups, deepest-index assignment, and added
slack groups from compressed-joint-cap-stress.md. Allow cap parameters
(v_ij,u_ij,b_ij) to vary, with fixed positive rho and

    sum_j rho_ij u_ij=0,
    C_ip=sum_j rho_ij(v_ij.p-b_ij)>=0

for every assigned index. These conditions preserve the whole-fiber cover.
At the initial parameter point normalize each cap continuous normal to unit
length. Put

    tau_j(z,x)=delta v_j.z+delta u_j.x-delta b_j.

At an ordinary facet point strictly inside the cap, the cap derivative's
body term is min_f r_f, so assign nonnegative owner weights alpha_jf with
sum_f alpha_jf=1. Outside the closed cap all owner weights are zero.
At a facet coinciding with the cap boundary there are two possibilities:

* If the original body is inside the cap, its outward normal is -u_j.
  The local derivative is min(min_f r_f, tau_j). Its gradient allocations
  satisfy alpha_jf>=0, sigma_j>=0, sum_f alpha_jf+sigma_j=1.
* If the original body is outside the cap, its outward normal is u_j.
  The local derivative is max(min_f r_f+tau_j,0). Its gradients are contained
  in the compact convex family alpha_jf>=0 and
  sum_f alpha_jf=sigma_j in [0,1], with local linear form
  sum_f alpha_jf r_f+sigma_j tau_j.

All these weights can depend measurably on x. On a proper cap section use
its ordinary (d-1)-dimensional measure; on a coincident facet use sigma_j
H_(d-1); on strictly full or empty fibers use zero section measure. Denote
the resulting effective section measure by nu_jz.

Each selected cap gradient has the form

    Gj(delta)=sum_(z,F,f) integral_F alpha_jf r_f
                +sum_z integral tau_j(z,x) dnu_jz(x).

Its admissible moment set is compact and convex. The actual cap directional
derivative is bounded ABOVE by the support function of this set: at every
point, one of the listed branch allocations realizes the actual derivative.
The same alpha and sigma must be used in the body and cap terms. Independent
choices of these terms would invalidate all subsequent moment identities.

## 4. Separation with a nonsmooth objective is still normalized

Let D be the finite-dimensional polyhedral tangent cone given by the active
linear projected coverage inequalities and the circuit-normal equations.
All body-plane coefficients are free. Define

    K=cone(union of all active cap-gradient sets)+D^polar,
    D^polar={ell: ell(delta)<=0 for every delta in D}.

Common fiber erosion is the body-plane variation delta b_f=-1,
delta a_f=delta n_f=0, with cap parameters fixed. It belongs to D and makes
every owner velocity -1. Every active cap contains a positive-area fiber
boundary patch strictly inside the cap. Thus erosion has uniformly negative
pairing with every gradient in every active cap-gradient set. It follows
that K is closed: pairing a convergent sequence in K with erosion bounds
the total nonnegative cap coefficient; compactness handles the cap part,
and the remaining polar part converges in its closed cone.

One must have G0 intersect K. Otherwise strict separation of the compact
convex G0 from the closed convex cone K gives delta in D with

    min_(g0 in G0) g0(delta)>0,
    max_(g in Gj) g(delta)<=0 for every active cap j.

Adding a sufficiently small positive amount of erosion keeps the objective
minimum positive and makes all cap bounds strictly negative. The actual
one-sided derivatives then yield, for small positive time, increased total
volume and every active cap below its fixed budget beta M. Slack caps stay
slack. The prescribed linear coverage remains valid. This contradicts the
attained depth minimum exactly as in the earlier joint variational problem.

Consequently, for one objective ownership allocation omega, selected cap
allocations alpha and sigma, and nonnegative lambda and eta, the normalized
stationarity identity holds. There is no abnormal objective multiplier:
the objective appears with coefficient one because it is an actual element
of G0 intersect K. The cap multipliers cannot all vanish; pair the identity
with joint continuous homothety as below.

## 5. New shared-plane signed moment equations

For each ambient BODY plane f define a signed facet measure, remembering
its integer coordinate, by

    dW_f(z,x)=(omega_f(z,x)-sum_j lambda_j alpha_jf(z,x))
                dH_(d-1)|F(x),

summed over its owned facet traces. Free variation of its threshold, integer
normal, and continuous normal gives respectively

    integral dW_f=0,
    integral z dW_f=0,
    integral x dW_f=0.

These are exact balance equations on every shared ambient plane. They have
no abstract support-compatibility multipliers. They retain, however, the
explicit owner allocations which are necessary at coincident restrictions.
It is unjustified to replace omega_f by 1 on every owned trace, or to force
all cap allocations to share the objective's owner partition.

All earlier cap-side equations survive unchanged. With

    S_ij=sum_z nu_ijz(R^d),
    Z_ij=sum_z z nu_ijz(R^d),
    X_ij=sum_z integral x dnu_ijz,
    t_i=sum_p eta_ip,

one has

    lambda_ij S_ij=rho_ij t_i,
    lambda_ij Z_ij=rho_ij sum_p eta_ip p,
    lambda_ij X_ij=rho_ij q_i.

Thus only at most 2^n groups carry stress, and each stressed group's full
effective sections have a common centroid, as in the rotating-circuit note.
The same contact, deepest-support, and full-rank apex conclusions follow.

Finally use joint continuous homothety: body (a_f,b_f) and cap (v_ij,b_ij)
scale together, with all continuous normals fixed. Every owner velocity on
a given facet agrees; every branch at a coincident cap also gives the same
homothety derivative. Hence EVERY g0 in G0 has value dM and EVERY cap-gradient
choice has value d mu(H_ij). Active homogeneous coverage and normal equations
pair to zero. Since stressed caps all have mass beta M, exactly

    sum_(i,j) lambda_ij=1/beta.

This gives a normalized global dual carrying both cap section-centroid
transport and shared-body-plane signed zeroth and first moments. An estimate
of a stressed group's multiplier sum by 1/gamma_d remains unproved.
